geometry_edits.rationale: Transform the dominant bent bar into a bifurcated mass to establish a clearer public threshold and stronger hierarchy.
Keep the split readable along the long axis so the gesture remains coherent in all views.
Introduce a controlled void between wings without fragmenting the overall mass.
Preserve continuity by retaining a bridge so the form does not become overly fragmented.
Add a true ground void to activate the frontage edge and support a public threshold.
Make the carved void the root so the public-space figure becomes a first-order spatial idea while retaining the mass ancestry.
Open the carve to the access side for a legible street response.
Tune the void size to read as usable public space rather than decorative subtraction.

graph_edits.rationale: Recast the dominant mass as a split-wing or bifurcated body to create a clearer public threshold and prevent the object from reading as a sealed bar.
Use a modest angular separation so the main mass remains one readable gesture while opening a legible seam toward the access edge.
Preserve smooth continuity in the dominant mass while introducing a controlled split rather than fragmented pieces.
Add a void-forming operation to generate a more legible public court or entry cut instead of relying on minor surface indentation.
Align the void to the verified access side so the ground response becomes publicly legible at the street edge.
Size the carved public space strongly enough to read across views without overwhelming the compact program volume.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent single mass in most views and the parcel containment appears respected, but the form is semantically underdeveloped for neighborhood living. It reads as a compact prismatic object with a slight bend/step, yet the visible void logic is weak: the blue frontage edge is not answered by a clear public court, entry seam, or undercut, so the access response feels sealed rather than active. Across views the silhouette remains readable, but the section does not strongly express an inhabitable ground threshold or a meaningful public-open space figure. It is therefore more of a generic compact mass with minor roof/profile articulation than a fully program-fit neighborhood street building.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The cited building reads as a taller mixed-use tower, so its vertical composition and urban scale are not directly transferable to this low-rise neighborhood-living candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact mass with a chamfered/stepped upper profile can stay legible while varying the silhouette; useful as a precedent for preserving one dominant volume with controlled roof articulation.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is a small restaurant/cafe object and its frontage logic is much more pavilion-like than this more capacity-aware neighborhood building.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple low horizontal base with a distinct vertical accent can clarify public fronting and program hierarchy.
